title: FAIL dossiers are content-free ('see audit-report.md') — the knowledge base records that a cycle failed but never why
notes: All six FAIL dossiers (1105/1106/1107/1115/1116/1117) carry byte-identical defects: [{id: audit-fail, severity: HIGH, summary: 'cycle did not pass audit; see audit-report.md + acs-verdict.json'}]. The dossier is the durable cross-cycle memory, yet it stores a POINTER to two files inside a run dir instead of the finding. Both inputs are already structured and available at write time: acs-verdict.json has red_ids, and audit-fail-reason.json has a reasons[] array. Carry the red predicate ids + the audit fail reason into the dossier so the next cycle's scout/triage can see WHAT failed without opening run artifacts. COVERAGE GAP in the naive fix: cycles 1105/1106 are agent-graded FAILs with red_count:0 / red_ids:null, so red_ids covers only the EGPS shape. A richer structured source already exists for those: the <!-- evolve-verdict: {...schema_version:2, failure:{class, defects[], evidence_paths[]}} --> trailer in audit-report.md (1105 line 131, 1106 line 152) carries full D1..D5 with file:line. Use that as the primary source. ORDERING: sequence AFTER acs-evidence-tail-capture — carrying red_ids into the dossier without fixing the excerpt just relocates a content-free pointer.
